stories.summary: CHEYENNE,. As intimated in the last dispatch, Gen. stories.headline: A FINE DAY'S RACING.; SOME FAST HORSES AT JEROME PARK. THE THREE-QUARTER DASH WON BY MADGE BRILLIANT VICTORY OF LIZZIE R. BELMONT'S FIDDLESTICK CAPTURES THE WITHERS STAKE ORE KNOB WINS THE MILE-AND-A-HALF DASH THE MILE-AND A-QUARTER RACE WON BY SPINDRIFT.
stories.summary: The opening day of the Jerome Park Spring Meeting was such a success as fine weather, large attendance, good running, and a reasonable number of victories for the favorites could make it. Five races were down on tho programme, in each a sufficient number of horses started to give variety and picturesqueness to the contests, and every race was well contested.

stories.summary: Vice Pres Humphrey urges concentrating on 'arts of peace,' s, Overseas Press Club, discussing foreign policy in gen; does not pull away from Johnson Adm record but appears to be starting to rebuild own identity in foreign affairs following Johnson announcement he will not seek re-election; says he thinks he will seek Dem nomination for Pres; replies to Fulbright charge of abuse of natl power

stories.headline: NIXON CALLS AIDES IN POSSIBLE MOVE ON IMPEACHMENT
stories.summary: Pres Nixon summons his chief defense atty James D St Clair, press sec Ronald L Ziegler, chief of staff Alexander M Haig Jr and speech writers Raymond K Price Jr and Patrick J Buchanan to Camp David, Md, arousing speculation that some new move is contemplated as result of Cong impeachment drive; deputy press sec Gerald L Warren says he knows of no plans for speech but does not rule out possibility that Nixon is preparing new response to pressures for impeachment; options open to Nixon noted; lr Sen R P Griffin sent to Pres Nixon warning that if Nixon defies Sen subpoenas for tapes Griffin will vote for conviction discussed; Repr J J Rhodes cancels news conf, in which he was to announce how he would vote on impeachment, because of illness (L)

stories.headline: All Europe Suddenly Focuses On the Political Crisis in U.S.
stories.summary: W Eur is swept by storm of intense reaction to Pres Nixon's latest disclosures in Watergate scandal; US pol crisis has suddenly eclipsed all other issues in public debate; Govt officials reluctant to comment publicly but press comment is most caustic in memory, some papers calling for Nixons resignation; several papers quoted (L)

stories.headline: CYPRUS FIGHTING RESUMES AS PEACE TALKS COLLAPSE; U.N. CALLED INTO SESSION
stories.summary: Fighting resumes on Cyprus shortly after peace talks break down in Geneva; Brit Sec James Callaghan calls for emergency meeting of UN Security Council; Turkish planes bomb Nicosia and area near airport; 2 hrs before attack, Turkish radio warns ships and civil aircraft to stay clear of area; AP and Reuters repts possibility that Greece is withdrawing from NATO; Greek Foreign Min George Mavros is quoted as saying 'NATO does not exist for Greece'; illus of Callaghan, Mavros and Turkish Foreign Min Turan Gunes leaving Geneva peace talks (S)

stories.headline: Poll Fear a Depression Is Ahead; Ford's Vow to Curb Inflation Stirs Hope
stories.summary: Gallup Poll taken 2 wks ago shows that 46% of those questioned fear US is headed for depression such as 1 experienced in '30s; total of 44% do not believe depression is coming, while other 10% have no opinion; finds that 68% of public believe econ situation will worsen over next 6 mos, while 13% think it will get better, 15% feel situation will be same and 4% have no opinion; NY Times survey conducted last wk finds that Pres Ford's vow to curb inflation offers hope; consumers, students, businessmen and housewives comment (L)
